chain.label: Route 4 charted beneath runway 33 approach path
chain.trigger: the FAA placed Helicopter Route 4 in close proximity to the runway 33 approach path at DCA without procedural mitigations to separate helicopter and fixed-wing traffic

chain.label: FAA failed to review routes or act on known midair risk
chain.trigger: the FAA ATO did not regularly review or reevaluate the route as required... the FAA failed to act on recommendations or available information to mitigate the identified risk

chain.label: Normalized overreliance on pilot-applied visual separation
chain.trigger: the air traffic system relied heavily on pilot-applied visual separation to maintain efficient traffic flow in the DCA terminal area, without adequate consideration of the inherent limitations of see-and-avoid

caused_by.evidence: controllers used visual separation because Route 4 was not procedurally separated from the runway 33 approach path
reliance contributed to a gradual normalization of using pilot-applied visual separation as the primary means of managing mixed helicopter and fixed-wing operations

chain.label: Army did not inform pilots of altimeter error tolerances
chain.trigger: the Army did not ensure that helicopter pilots were adequately informed about the effects of allowable error tolerances in barometric altimeters

chain.label: Barometric altimeter indicated ~100 ft low
chain.trigger: the crew of PAT25 observed a barometric altimeter altitude about 100 ft lower than the helicopter's true altitude, due to additive allowable instrument and ESSS position error

chain.label: PAT25 flying above published maximum route altitude
chain.trigger: the accident helicopter crew was flying above the published maximum route altitude; last recorded radio altitude 278 ft against a 200-ft Route 4 maximum

caused_by.evidence: the Army's failure to ensure pilots were aware of the effects of error tolerances on barometric altimeters, which resulted in the crew flying above the maximum published helicopter route altitude
the crew erroneously believing that they were under the published maximum altitude for Route 4

chain.label: Night operations against complex city lighting
chain.trigger: both flight crews were operating under conditions that made visual acquisition of the other aircraft difficult, including nighttime operations, a complex background of city lights, and limited relative motion between the aircraft

chain.label: Traffic alerting limitations on both aircraft
chain.trigger: the limitations of the traffic awareness and collision alerting systems on both aircraft, which precluded effective alerting of the impending collision; TCAS RAs were inhibited below 900 ft and the helicopter had no integrated CDTI

caused_by.evidence: the FAA's failure across multiple organizations to implement previous NTSB recommendations, including ADS-B In

chain.label: Helicopter and local control positions kept combined
chain.trigger: the LC and HC positions were combined and staffed by a CPC during a period of elevated traffic volume, with no structured risk assessment process to support real-time operational decision making

caused_by.evidence: the absence of a risk assessment process to identify and mitigate real-time operational risk factors

chain.label: Degraded and blocked radio transmissions to PAT25
chain.trigger: the helicopter's CVR did not contain the word 'circling'; one of the helicopter pilots pressed the push-to-talk switch for 0.8 seconds, blocking 'two five pass behind that'

chain.label: Tower team loss of situation awareness; no advisory or safety alert
chain.trigger: high workload at the DCA ATCT degraded controller performance and situation awareness... misprioritization of duties, incomplete traffic advisories, and the lack of safety alerts to both flight crews

caused_by.evidence: the combination of the helicopter control and local control positions during a period of elevated traffic volume... contributed to misprioritization of duties

chain.label: IP requested visual separation without identifying flight 5342
chain.trigger: the lack of effective pilot-applied visual separation by the helicopter crew; the IP reported 'traffic in sight' and requested visual separation without positively identifying the airplane

caused_by.evidence: crews frequently initiated a request for visual separation when traffic was pointed out; requesting visual separation before visually acquiring traffic had become normalized
flight 5342 was one of five airplanes approaching DCA in darkness from the south, appearing as points of light near the horizon
the crew did not receive information about the airplane's circling approach to a different runway, which reinforced an incorrect expectation that the airplane did not pose a conflict
the controller merely asked if the PAT25 crew had the 'C-R-J in sight' without providing position information to direct the visual search

chain.label: IP never called out the airplane's position to the pilot flying
chain.trigger: the IP did not verbally discuss with the pilot the location of flight 5342 after either traffic call; instead he said 'kinda come left for me ma'am, I think that's why he's asking'

caused_by.evidence: he was uncertain about the airplane's position and assumed it was among the airplanes on approach to runway 1

chain.label: PAT25 and flight 5342 collide at 278 ft msl
chain.trigger: the aircraft collided over the Potomac River at an altitude about 278 ft above mean sea level, about 0.5 miles southeast of DCA

caused_by.evidence: the helicopter's flight path crossed the runway 33 approach corridor above the published route altitude
the airplane crew did not detect the helicopter until about 1 second before impact
neither crew received technological cues sufficient to overcome the limitations of visual scanning in this environment
the lack of safety alerts to both flight crews that could have resulted in flight crew actions to avert the collision
the lack of effective pilot-applied visual separation by the helicopter crew, which resulted in a midair collision
no crew discussion of the conflicting traffic occurred before impact

chain.label: Both aircraft impact the Potomac River and are destroyed
chain.trigger: impacted the Potomac River in southwest Washington, DC... Both aircraft were destroyed as a result of the accident

caused_by.evidence: wreckage of both aircraft was located in the Potomac River near the approach end of runway 33

chain.label: 67 fatalities
chain.trigger: The 2 pilots, 2 flight attendants, and 60 passengers on board the airplane and all 3 crewmembers on board the helicopter died

caused_by.evidence: cause of death was multiple blunt force injuries for all occupants examined
both aircraft were destroyed on impact with the river
